Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect both required wake views and the fish-control bookshelf before touching the policy. After that I’ll trace the parent/inherited evidence, implement one candidate, and update both required evidence files.

I’m using the required wake-visual skill to structure the two-view diagnosis, and the fish-control-primitives skill because this is an architecture decision from the inherited candidate. I’ll read both instruction sets completely before inspecting or editing the policy.

The inherited candidate already contains a course servo plus terminal half-cycle reallocation, so this is not the common naive seed despite the lineage origin. I’m now comparing the closest-approach rollout against the best finite-score rollout and the other sampled failures, including initialization, forces, saturation, and trajectory topology.

The visual evidence is consistent across views: all four swimmers self-propel with coherent alternating 3D wakes. The earlier controllers hold a nearly straight leftward course and miss high by about 3L; the course-servo descendants bend downward, improve closest approach to 1.27–1.55L, then continue/coast below the target into the lower boundary. I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a compact steering realization that preserves the carrier instead of adding scalar cadence tuning.

The shelf points to one appropriate invariant for this failure: preserve the traveling bend and use a response-conditioned redirect/release near capture, based on observed geometry and body response—not elapsed time. Before choosing its exact translation, I found deeper inherited optimizer logs and am reading those now so I don’t repeat the already-falsified cadence, half-cycle, or mean-curvature variants.

The inherited sequence now rules out three tempting repeats: cadence relief worsened the direct course-servo near miss, carrier attenuation improved one pass but quenched the wake, and both carrier-preserving mean curvature and an energy guard still ended in the same lower-exit class. I’m recording a distinct hypothesis before editing: preserve the full traveling carrier and add distance-gated inertial line-of-sight-rate feedforward to the existing body-frame course servo, so the terminal turn persists through beat-scale course oscillations.

The policy now keeps the full carrier and changes only the terminal guidance signal; outside 4L it is algebraically identical to the prefill’s course servo. I’m adding the durable negative lesson next: rhythm preservation alone did not improve the lower-exit class, so future work must separate carrier health from terminal interception.

Both required files are now materially updated. I’m moving through the lightweight checks: guidance materiality, Julia policy contract, mirrored-state/reflection behavior, and editable-boundary integrity. No CFD will be run.

The guidance check passed. The Julia check is currently blocked by the shell environment (`julia` is not on `PATH`), not by a policy assertion; I’m checking the workspace/module configuration for the expected binary before falling back to the checker’s static contract audit.

The contract passes with the workspace’s Julia 1.10.9 binary, and the editable-boundary check passes. I’m doing two final algebraic audits before the mandated checker: exact far-field equivalence to the prefill and reflection symmetry of the new terminal signal.

The algebraic audits pass: the new policy is exactly identical to the prefill outside 4L, is reflection-equivariant, and keeps returned accelerations bounded. Per the workspace contract, I’m now invoking the dedicated check runner for an independent no-CFD validation.

The independent check runner reports all three mandated checks PASS, including the deterministic parameter-schema guard and solver boundary; it confirms no CFD was run. I’m recording those non-CFD audits in the candidate notes and then doing one final content/line-location review.

Produced exactly one candidate: `dogfish3d_course_servo_terminal_los_feedforward_v1`.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:8): preserves the full traveling carrier and adds distance-gated line-of-sight-rate feedforward.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records the two-view diagnosis, inherited negative results, bookshelf transfer, hypothesis, and falsification boundary.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:49): adds the reusable distinction between carrier preservation and terminal-intercept guidance.

All mandated checks passed: guidance materiality, Julia contract/schema, far-field equivalence, reflection symmetry, bounded actions, and editable boundary. No CFD was run.
